findings.evidence: Laurent/Resolution.lean:85-88 `toUngraded ... : ExactK0 (E.fullSubcategory R hR hRshift).toExactStructure ≃+ ExactK0 (E.toExactStructure.fullSubcategory R hR)` and :102-108, whose proof (`induction r with | base => simp | step ... => simp [ih]`) is character-for-character the one at Resolving.lean:101-109. `resolvingSubcategory P` is an `abbrev` for `E.fullSubcategory P IsResolving.isExtensionClosed` (Exact/Resolving.lean:96), so the types coincide. The needed `LocallySmall.{w} C` comes free from `EssentiallySmall.{w} C` (mathlib/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/EssentiallySmall.lean:126) and `ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall P` is already the local instance at Resolving.lean:73.
findings.fix: Move the general `Transport` section (parameterized by `R`, `hR`, `hRshift`) out of Laurent/Resolution.lean into a shared module importable by both (e.g. a new `Laurent/FullSubcategory.lean` importing `Exact.Graded.FullSubcategory`, `Laurent.Basic`, `GrothendieckGroup.Resolution`), drop `private`, and instantiate it here at `hR := IsResolving.isExtensionClosed`.
findings.issue: `toUngraded`, `toUngraded_of`, `toUngraded_symm_of` and `ofExactK0_toUngraded_symm_eulerClassFullSubcategory` (lines 84-109) re-prove at `R := P` the general transport of Laurent/Resolution.lean:85-108, which is stated for an arbitrary extension-closed, shift-stable `R`; the copies here are stated under the stronger `[E.toExactStructure.IsResolving P]` although the arguments use only `hP` and `hshift`.

findings.evidence: Both `map_smul'` proofs are the identical `simp only [AddEquiv.toFun_eq_coe, resolutionAddEquiv_apply, map_smul, RingHom.id_apply]` (Resolving.lean:142-143, Resolution.lean:163-164); no such general helper exists — grep for `LinearEquiv` in GrothendieckGroup/ finds only `mapEquiv`, `forgetGradingEquiv` (Laurent/Basic.lean:371, :514).
findings.fix: State that once in Laurent/Basic.lean beside `map`/`mapEquiv`, e.g. `LaurentK0.linearEquivOfMap (h : GradedConflationExact E E' F) (e : LaurentK0 E ≃+ LaurentK0 E') (he : ∀ x, e x = map h x) : LaurentK0 E ≃ₗ[LaurentPolynomial ℤ] LaurentK0 E'` with a `toLinearMap = map h` lemma, and derive both `laurentResolutionEquiv`s from it.
findings.issue: `resolutionAddEquiv`, `resolutionAddEquiv_apply`, the `map_smul'` field of `laurentResolutionEquiv` and `laurentResolutionEquiv_toLinearMap` (lines 112-155) repeat the same upgrade argument as Laurent/Resolution.lean:128-176. The underlying fact has nothing to do with resolutions: an `AddEquiv` of `LaurentK0`s whose function is `LaurentK0.map h` for a graded conflation-exact `h` is automatically `ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`-linear.

findings.evidence: Resolution.lean:203-207 and Resolving.lean:187-194 quantify over arbitrary `r : FiniteResolution P X`, `s : FiniteResolution P (E.shift.functor.obj X)` and assert the same equation; `IsExtensionClosed` is a `Prop` (Exact/ExtensionClosed.lean:88), so the two `hP` witnesses make the statements defeq. `ExactStructure.isResolving_isProjective` (Exact/Resolving.lean:122) gives hypothesis sets where both fire.
findings.fix: Factor the shift covariance into a single lemma over a `ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`-linear equivalence whose inverse computes Euler classes (hypotheses: `e.symm (of _ X) = r.foldAlternating _` and the same for `X{1}`), and derive both named theorems from it, so only one proof of the shift covariance exists.
findings.issue: `foldAlternating_shift_eq_T_one_smul` has the same conclusion, in the same type `LaurentK0 (E.fullSubcategory P hP hshift)`, as `GradedExactStructure.foldAlternating_shift_eq_T_one_smul` (Laurent/Resolution.lean:203); both are applicable, and indistinguishable to a user, whenever `P = E.isProjective` is resolving.

summary: The public statements are at the right level and the hypotheses are the natural ones, but the module re-proves at the special case P the graded/ungraded transport and the AddEquiv-to-LinearEquiv upgrade that Laurent/Resolution.lean already proves for an arbitrary extension-closed shift-stable R (kept private), and its shift-covariance theorem duplicates the conclusion of the existing one. Hoist the general machinery into a shared module and instantiate it in both files.
